perspective:
Sara Manuelito’s accessible information:

- She is Sara Manuelito, an American Indian woman, a Speech-Language Pathologist with primary education and an INTP personality.
- Shirley Whiteplume is her long-time colleague and close friend; they work together at a community health center and have several years of shared professional and personal experience.
- They shared care for a mutual patient who has died. Sara attended the patient’s funeral. Sara knows they made treatment decisions for him and provided care; she recalls the good care and moments of joy they brought him.
- At the funeral, Sara observed Shirley’s somber demeanor and suspected Shirley was deeply affected. Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and that she saw how much Shirley cared. Shirley said it had been tough and she kept thinking if more could have been done. Sara said they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy. Shirley replied, “You’re right. It’s just hard to let go.”
- On a coffee break, Sara raised the patient’s treatment decisions because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley said she appreciated that but it was hard to accept.
- In a quiet office moment, Sara observed Shirley being reserved and holding back emotion. Sara confronted her, saying it was okay to be open. Shirley said she didn’t want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotion doesn’t make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Later, Sara thought her previous confrontation might have been too harsh. She apologized if she came on too strong. Shirley said it was a bit much but Sara meant well, and she appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better and felt hopeful. Sara asked how she was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggested spending more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and said they should plan something for the weekend.

Sara does not have access to Shirley’s private thoughts except as Shirley expressed them or as Sara observed/inferred them.
